tip: Turkish states the percent first: 'yüzde doksan beş' is literally in-hundred ninety-five, meaning 95 percent.
Comparison uses the from-ending '-den' plus 'daha': 'benden daha uzun' means taller than me.
'söz vermek' joins the noun 'söz' (word) with 'vermek' (give) to mean promise, not literally to give a word.
'temizletti' is 'temizle' (clean) plus the make-someone ending '-t': make someone clean. 'bana' marks the person made to do it.
The '-muş' in 'unutmuşum' marks something noticed after the fact: I seem to have forgotten, not a plain I forgot.
'uyumadan önce' means before sleeping: a verb stem plus '-madan önce' builds before doing something.
'koşarak' is 'koş' (run) plus '-arak', meaning by running or while running: it says how the main action happened.
'annemin yaptığı' means the one my mom makes: '-dığı' builds a describing phrase, and the doer 'annem' takes '-in'.
'olsaydık' paired with 'yapmazdık' is the past what-if form: if we had been, we would not have made it.
'sorar' uses the habitual ending '-ar', matching 'her akşam' (every evening): things done regularly.
'çaldığında' means when it rings: add '-dığında' to a verb stem to say at the time something happens.
'annemden' uses the from-ending '-den' to mark the source you learn from: learned from my mother.
'olmalı' adds '-malı' to 'ol-', meaning should or must be: it states obligation or a firm opinion.
'gelince' means once it comes: '-ince' attaches to a verb stem for as soon as something happens.
'oluşturmaktadır' is the formal '-makta' present: much the same meaning as '-yor' but used in official or written Turkish.
'vapurla' is 'vapur' (ferry) plus '-la', the by or with ending: by ferry, with no separate word for by needed.
'ne kadar' paired with 'o kadar' frames 'the more, the more': 'ne kadar çok egzersiz, o kadar iyi'.
'hoşlanmak', to enjoy, needs the from-ending '-tan' on what you enjoy. 'yapmaktan hoşlanırım' means enjoy from doing.
The at-ending '-de' marks a timeframe, so 'otuz günde' means within thirty days, not on day thirty.
The '-er' ending plus '-di' makes a used-to past: 'çekerdi' means used to draw, a repeated action long ago.
'zorunda kalmak' means to be forced to and follows the base '-mek' form. 'yürümek zorunda kaldı' means had to walk.
'ne olursa olsun' is a fixed phrase for no matter what. 'hava ne olursa olsun' means whatever the weather.
The suffix '-meli' means should or must, as in 'yemeliler', they should eat.
'-saydın' with a would-form builds a past what-if: 'çalışsaydın' then 'geçerdin' means had you studied, you would have passed.
Possession links two words. 'komşunun' takes the owner-ending '-nun' and 'tavukları' takes '-ları', the neighbor's chickens.
Repeating a word intensifies it. 'taze taze' means all fresh or freshly, stressing manner.
The frame '-se de' and '-mese de' means whether or not. 'istesem de istemesem de' means whether I want to or not.
'-se' on a verb makes an open if. 'öğrensem' means if I learn, with the outcome still possible.
'-dığım' turns a verb into that I did. 'aldığım çilekler' means the strawberries that I bought.
'-ken' added to a verb means while. 'gelirken' means while coming, marking the background action.
